hypothesis: Pigment-network states are repeatedly reachable through regulatory/flux changes
chun_result_basis: 8/8 independent mechanistic clusters show regulatory/flux evidence; 6/6 red-direction clusters show higher anthocyanin; no positive structural-loss requirement in informative clusters
claim_boundary: supports recurrent accessibility, not a natural mechanism frequency

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like red/pink floral state generally enables colder climatic niche expansion in Camellia
chun_result_basis: exact-taxonomy 50-species A vs W: BIO1 P=0.785; BIO6 P=0.554; cold-tail P=0.697; specimen-only P=0.746/0.586/0.527; OpenTree/Grafen BM-PGLS on 33 taxa: BIO1 P=0.361, BIO6 median P=0.070, cold-tail P=0.614; colder C. rusticana is not visibly redder than C. japonica
claim_boundary: do not retain as a genus-wide primary hypothesis

hypothesis: Anthocyanin deployment facilitates cold/UV adaptation only in particular lineages or ecological contexts
chun_result_basis: macro literature contains support, null and counterexample units; genus-wide A-W thermal mean is null; topology-aware BIO6 has only a weak non-significant cold-direction trend
remaining_test: primary nuclear-tree branch-event lead/lag tests; mechanistic pigment rather than visible hue
claim_boundary: plausible only conditionally; present data do not identify causal branches

hypothesis: Yellow state is unusually historically/geographically constrained
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 species analysis: Y 22/22 confined to South China/Southwest China/Vietnam versus non-Y 64/84; one-sided Fisher P=0.00552; A vs W geography P=1.0; GBIF thermal Y sample remains only two South-China Chrysantha species
remaining_test: nuclear-tree ancestral range/transition reconstruction and broader occurrence audit
claim_boundary: supports geographic constraint, not a yellow thermal optimum

hypothesis: Red/pink anthocyanin-like state expands beyond southern ancestral belt more readily than white
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 species geography: A 21/28 south-only vs W 43/56; OR=0.907, Fisher P=1.0
claim_boundary: A and W are indistinguishable in this source-geography contrast

hypothesis: Visible flower-colour states are strongly structured by lineage/history rather than being distributed independently across Camellia
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 deterministic species table excluding non-section Vietnam rows: 98 species across 17 traditional sections; section×colour Pearson chi2=178.646, Cramer's V=0.955, 100000-shuffle permutation P<1e-5; e.g. sect. Camellia 22/23 A, sect. Chrysantha 13/13 Y, sect. Thea 14/14 W
remaining_test: replace traditional-section proxy with admitted nuclear-tree phylogenetic signal / transition model
claim_boundary: traditional sections are not assumed monophyletic; result establishes strong taxonomic-history structure, not a quantified nuclear phylogenetic signal

hypothesis: Molecular accessibility generates variants while ecology/history filters which states persist macroevolutionarily
chun_result_basis: strong micro recurrence contrasts with weak macro cold-enabler evidence; P(micro regulatory recurrence > macro cold-enabler support)=0.9725; exact-taxonomy/specimen-only/topology-aware A-W thermal results do not support a universal red=cold mapping; yellow geography and section-colour structure are strong
remaining_test: micro-accessibility score -> macro reuse -> environmental/pollinator persistence model
claim_boundary: supported as synthesis pattern; causal filtering factors not yet separated

hypothesis: The exact pigment-network nodes labile within development/cultivars are preferentially reused on macroevolutionary colour-transition branches
chun_result_basis: cross-scale accessibility pattern motivates this but macro branch gene assignments are not yet available
remaining_test: primary nuclear tree + transition mapping + raw RNAseq/common ortholog node enrichment

hypothesis: Pollinator sensory environment helps determine which accessible pigment/spectral states persist
chun_result_basis: species-level pollination evidence is heterogeneous; same visible red can be bird-associated or insect-associated
remaining_test: phylogenetic meta-regression on spectrum/UV, nectar, season and effective pollination
claim_boundary: do not infer from human colour categories alone

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like A lineages occupy narrower thermal breadth than W lineages
chun_result_basis: OpenTree synthetic topology + Grafen BM-PGLS: BIO1 IQR A-W=-1.17 C, P=0.000233; raw exact-taxonomy and specimen-only species-label tests are non-significant (P=0.627 and 0.748)
remaining_test: primary dated nuclear tree and occurrence-definition sensitivity
claim_boundary: do not promote from topology-only sensitivity; direction is opposite to an A-enabled niche-expansion prediction

hypothesis: Human-visible W/A/Y states merge distinct biochemical, sensory and ecological states and therefore lose macroevolutionarily relevant information
chun_result_basis: visible colour is weak for exact 50-species thermal axes; most directly, red C. japonica and red C. rusticana have different pollination strategies and strongly different thermal niches; mechanistic ledger shows multiple regulatory/flux routes to superficially similar less-red/white states and yellow C. nitidissima combines flavonol and carotenoid deployment. The initial section-vs-colour cold-tail contrast is excluded as supporting evidence because leave-one-section-out shows it is dominated by Tuberculatae.
remaining_test: build species latent pigment/spectral state matrix and compare predictive/phylogenetic fit against W/A/Y on primary nuclear trees
claim_boundary: supports visible hue as a lossy deterministic proxy, not yet superiority of a particular latent-state model

hypothesis: White is often an accessible retained-pathway reservoir/bridge rather than a terminal pigment-loss state
chun_result_basis: published visible root is white; exact climate subset W spans 9/10 observed sections versus A 2/10 and Y 1/10; all informative mechanistic clusters implicate regulatory/flux changes and none require wholesale structural loss
remaining_test: nuclear-tree stochastic maps with root/state-frequency/sampling controls plus pathway-retention evidence on W->coloured branches
claim_boundary: broad white distribution can arise by ancestral retention alone; do not call white an evolutionary hub until transition centrality exceeds null expectation

hypothesis: Ecological function can change while coarse visible hue remains similar
chun_result_basis: red C. japonica is bird-associated whereas red C. rusticana is insect-associated; C. rusticana is much colder in BIO1/BIO6/cold-tail despite sharing the red visible label
remaining_test: expand spectra/UV/pollinator/niche matrix across independent same-hue species pairs and test phylogenetically
claim_boundary: one strong within-genus case establishes non-uniqueness of hue-to-function mapping, not its genus-wide frequency

hypothesis: Extreme climatic range limits are generated by rare lineage-specific boundary shifts rather than broad visible-colour regimes
chun_result_basis: the initial section model for BIO6 q05 has R2=0.418 P=0.005, but removing Tuberculatae drops it to R2=0.206 P=0.291 and reverses AIC preference; the two white Tuberculatae taxa have mean BIO6 q05=-15.26 C versus -1.41 C in the other 32 W taxa
remaining_test: audit the exact GBIF/specimen coordinates and taxonomy for Tuberculatae; then test lower-niche-limit branch shifts on primary nuclear trees
claim_boundary: candidate only: the extreme tail may reflect genuine tolerance, geography, sampling or occurrence/taxonomic artefact
